# XPath expression built from HTTP request data (Python)

`qualor:python/xpath-injection` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-643](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/643.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A05:2025 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A05_2025-Injection/), [A03:2021 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A03_2021-Injection/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data built into an XPath expression: lxml's `xpath()`, `etree.XPath()` and
`XPathEvaluator`, and the paths of ElementTree's (or defusedxml's) `find()`, `findall()`,
`findtext()` and `iterfind()`, in Flask, Django and FastAPI applications. Values passed as XPath
variables (keyword arguments of `xpath()`) are fine and not reported.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
Quotes and operators in the value change the query. A name such as `' or '1'='1` turns
`//user[@name='...']` into a query that matches every user, which can bypass a login check or
reveal other users' data.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the name is pasted into the XPath expression.

```python
from flask import Flask, jsonify, request
from lxml import etree

app = Flask(__name__)
USERS = etree.parse("users.xml")


@app.route("/email")
def email():
    name = request.args["name"]
    found = USERS.xpath("//user[@name='" + name + "']/email/text()")
    return jsonify(emails=[str(e) for e in found])
```

**Compliant:** the expression is constant and the name is an XPath variable.

```python
from flask import Flask, jsonify, request
from lxml import etree

app = Flask(__name__)
USERS = etree.parse("users.xml")


@app.route("/email")
def email():
    found = USERS.xpath("//user[@name=$name]/email/text()", name=request.args["name"])
    return jsonify(emails=[str(e) for e in found])
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Keep the expression constant and pass request values as XPath variables:
  `tree.xpath("//user[@name=$name]", name=value)` (also with `etree.XPath`).
- ElementTree's `find()` family has no variables: pick the path from a fixed allow-list, or
  iterate and compare in Python (`[u for u in root.iter("user") if u.get("name") == value]`).
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Flask
- Django
- FastAPI
- lxml
- `xml.etree.elementtree`
- defusedxml

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- A slice is followed when it slices request data in place (`request.args["q"][:50]`),
  a variable assigned request data, or a view parameter; a slice of a value built from request
  data (`(request.args["q"] + "x")[:50]`), or of a variable assigned again after the request value
  (`q = q.strip()`), is missed.
- `xpath()` is checked on any receiver in a module that imports lxml at the top level; a module
  that imports lxml only inside `try:` or under `if TYPE_CHECKING:` gets no `xpath()` findings.
- `find()` and its relatives are checked only on a tree or element the rule can see being parsed or
  created; a tree from a helper, a parameter, an attribute, a loop or a result list is missed.
- An allow-list is recognised only as a lookup in a module-level dict of literals assigned to an
  upper-case name that is never changed, or as a ternary of constants; a membership check is not.
- Request sources are recognised by their shape: a Flask `<int:n>` route parameter and a numeric
  Django URL argument still count as request data, and a function whose first parameter is named
  `request` in a Django module is taken for a view.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/python/xpath/xpath-injection.py`](../../../rules/python/xpath/xpath-injection.py) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.

The rule: [`rules/python/xpath/xpath-injection.yml`](../../../rules/python/xpath/xpath-injection.yml), added in version 2026.10.1.
